A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpecPrefill research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongBench, RULER, short-task, and inference-efficiency experiments, including component ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluated baselines, longer-context RULER results, and a comparative latency experiment.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same speculative token-selection procedure: look-ahead, attention aggregation, smoothing and chunk selection, and restoration of positional information. No model component or inference step changes.

E1.justification: RULER coverage extends from 4K–32K contexts in v1 Table 1 to include 64K and 128K in v2 Table 2, adding longer-input test scenarios. The benchmark families, task categories, and short-task coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds actual LongBench comparisons with LLMLingua and MInference, and Figure 5 adds a latency comparison with MInference. This substantially broadens comparisons beyond the base model and custom sentence-RAG baselines. Both original RAG variants remain in Appendix B and the renumbered Figure 7.

E3.justification: The added comparisons specify context-only compression for LLMLingua and MInference's officially searched attention pattern. The new latency experiment uses eight H100s with TP=8 and batch/length configurations through 8×64K and 4×128K. These are added protocols; the existing H200 timing experiments and their settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 5 extends the efficiency sensitivity analysis by comparing dense attention, MInference, and SpecPrefill across batch-size/context-length combinations. The existing chunk-selection and look-ahead ablations remain unchanged, including the appendix plots.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. The added results do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 substantially extends the comparative results: Table 1 reports MInference's LongBench average of 52.89 and LLMLingua results alongside SpecPrefill's 52.74 at 10% retention. Table 2 adds 64K/128K RULER averages excluding aggregation: 90.4/65.6 for SpecPrefill versus 87.9/60.3 for the baseline. Figure 5 adds comparative latency curves. Shared 4K–32K RULER values and the retained plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: The attention-score definition, aggregation procedure, and Appendix E FLOPS and overhead calculations are unchanged. The theoretical speedup plots and formulas are renumbered, with no new theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: training-free token selection using a smaller model, up to 7× maximum QPS and 7.66× TTFT speedup, and compatibility with speculative decoding. The added comparisons supply evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly identifies potential multi-turn conversation failure without context recomputation and discusses the resulting KV-cache trade-off. Sections 2.3 and 4.7.2 also expand the explanation of tensor-parallel communication costs and why relative efficiency depends on batch size and context length.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added baselines' processing choices and identifies eight H100s with TP=8 for the new latency comparison. Existing implementation details in Appendices C–D remain. The code-access footnote changes from the named Jingyu6 repository to an anonymous repository address; the PDFs do not establish that address's usability.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for FlexPrefill, Hip Attention, SampleAttention, another context-compression work, and SCBench. It also corrects the vLLM attribution to Kwon et al. and removes the previously misattributed SnapKV reference. These changes refine the existing positioning against sparse attention and compression methods.

P1.justification: v2 creates a separate baselines-and-variants subsection from material previously inside the LongBench subsection, revises parts of the background, and moves the impact statement after the conclusion. Abstract copyedits and publication-header changes are local; most prose and the appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the LongBench comparison table and MInference latency plot, expands the RULER table with additional rows, and relocates the existing timing heatmaps. Other figures and appendix tables retain their visual content apart from numbering and associated references.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's base-model and custom-RAG comparisons, v2 provides stronger peer-method validation through LLMLingua and MInference, tests longer contexts, and explicitly identifies a multi-turn limitation. These additions improve assessment of practical trade-offs. The benefit is tempered by the anonymized code pointer and a small reporting inconsistency: Section 4.7.2 states 99.5% quality retention, whereas Table 1 and Figure 5 indicate about 99.7%.
